PHILIP MORRIS U. S. A.
INTER-OFFICE CORRESPONDENCE
RICHMOND, VIRGINIA
To:
Mr. T. A. Newman
Date: July 31, 1981
C81- 05224
From:
C. L. Irving
Subject:
Evaluation of Borgwaldt Firmness Tester
The evaluation of the Borgwaldt Firmness Tester will determine:
1) If the Borgwaldt unit is as sensitive to cigarette firmness
as the standard PM compacimer,
2) If the variability of the Borgwaldt instrument is comparable
to that of the PM compacimeter,
3) If the Borgwaldt unit is unduly sensitive to other cigarette
characteristics such as circumference or seam orientation, and
4) If the unit is easier to operate, set-up and maintain than the
standard PM compacimeter.
The sensitivity and variability of the Borgwaldt unit will be
determined by testing cigarettes of a single blend at five different
weight levels on both the Borgwaldt instrument and the PM compacimeter.
This portion of the experiment will be performed three times to ensure
the accuracy of the results. Cigarettes will also be tested at two
circumference levels and five weight levels to determine the sensitivity
of the Borgwaldt unit to circumference variation. In addition, a set of
cigarettes will be tested with three different seam orientations to
determine the sensitivity of Borgwaldt firmness results to seam position.
The data from these experiments will be analyzed to determine the sensi-
tivity and variability of the Borgwaldt instrument so it can be compared
with the PM compacimeter.
The experience gained while performing the tests outlined above
should provide a good indication of the ease with which the Borgwaldt
instrument can be set-up and operated. The determination of the
maintainability of the unit is strictly an engineering judgement.
The evaluation of the Borgwaldt firmness tester, as outlined above,
should require approximately two months to complete after receipt of the
instrument. If you have any questions about this test procedure or any
suggestions for additions to the program, please, let me know.
